comparisons.peer_topic: Changes in Allowance for Credit Losses and Provision Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: The allowance for credit losses decreased $215 million to $14.3 billion in 2024, driven by decreases in commercial and consumer real estate portfolios, while the provision for credit losses increased $1.4 billion to $5.8 billion primarily due to credit card and small business loan growth and commercial real estate office asset quality deterioration.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclose changes in their Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) driven by credit card and consumer loan growth. Citi attributes its ACL increase to 'cards loan growth' and macroeconomic pressures, while Bank of America notes an increase in the credit card portfolio offsetting declines in other areas, with provision increases also driven by 'credit card... loan growth'. However, Citi's total consumer ACL increased to $16.0 billion, whereas Bank of America's total ACL decreased to $14.3 billion, with Bank of America specifically citing decreases in commercial and consumer real estate portfolios as a counterbalance to credit card growth.

sentences.text: Citi's total consumer allowance for credit losses on loans (ACLL) as of December 31, 2024 was $16,018 million, an increase from $15,431 million at December 31, 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by the impact of macroeconomic pressures related to the elevated inflationary and interest rate environment, as well as cards loan growth.
The allowance for credit losses decreased $215 million from December 31, 2023 to $14.3 billion at December 31, 2024.

The decline in the allowance for credit losses was attributed to decreases in the commercial portfolio of $240 million and the consumer real estate portfolio of $118 million, partially offset by an increase in the credit card and other consumer portfolios of $143 million.

The increase in provision for credit losses in 2024 was primarily driven by credit card as well as small business loan growth, and asset quality deterioration in the commercial real estate office and credit card portfolios.
